business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Second largest (No. 2) selling wood adhesive (white glue) brand in India's retail segment under the 'Euro 7000' brand, launched in 2006.
- Present across 14 states via 56 branches and 65 distributors, reaching 13,000 retailers and 3.5 lac carpenters through a 455-strong sales force.
- Onboarded actor Pankaj Tripathi in 2025 as National Brand Ambassador, running a new 360-degree campaign (#SirfJodoNahinFayedonKeSaathJodo) live across TV, Print, OOH and Digital since Q1FY26 to strengthen national brand visibility and trade confidence.
- Vision is to acquire national leadership in wood adhesives in the retail segment and become India's most preferred adhesive brand for carpenters.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Retail contributes ~94% of revenue; OEM segment currently ~6% with target to reach 15% in 2-3 years. Geographic mix shifting from Gujarat/Maharashtra stronghold to new states (UP, Delhi, WB, Odisha, Chhattisgarh).

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable for B2C adhesive model; performance tracked via monthly volume run-rates (March hit >2,100 tons).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 15-20% volume CAGR targeted for next 2-3 years to reach INR 500cr; Margin: Sustainable EBITDA band of 23-25% (Gross Margin ~65%); Order Inflow: Focus on tertiary offtake via carpenter engagement; Capex: Brownfield expansion completing in 1-2 quarters (capacity 2,000 -> 3,500 tons/month).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Untapped market share in mature states (only ~1/3 retail outlets penetrated in Mumbai); expansion into 2 new states in May '26; OEM segment scaling in metro cities; long-term vision to reach INR 1,000-1,200cr revenue.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin target 65%; EBITDA target 23-25%. Pressure from VAM prices doubling (INR 75-80 to INR 160-180/kg); management passed through 60-70% of cost hike via price increases effective May 1st. Advertising intensity increasing from 4% to 6-7% of revenue.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing reinvestment for growth (brand building, capacity, working capital). Maintaining ~15% dividend payout. No buybacks planned; cash held in FDs/Liquid funds to support expansion and cover INR 95cr carpenter bonus liability.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic and aggressive on market share capture; transparent about working capital stretch being a strategic choice for new market entry; confident in passing on raw material costs; focused on 'transformation journey' from distributor-led to brand-led model.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Working Capital: Receivable days stretched to 150-160 days (vs normal 120) due to new state entry; Raw Materials: VAM price volatility linked to crude/geopolitics; Competition: New capacity additions by peers in Gujarat; Demand: Potential short-term demand destruction from sharp price hikes, though management sees limited impact as adhesives are small % of total furniture cost.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'carpenter bonus liability' of ~INR 95cr acts as a unique working capital feature, effectively an interest-free float from the channel that funds part of the cash balance. The company is deliberately stretching receivables in new states for 2-3 years to build relationships, accepting lower cash conversion temporarily for market share.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising VAM prices and need for continuous price pass-through | Unorganized Local Adhesive Manufacturers | loser | High | Lack pricing power and hedging capabilities to absorb 100% VAM spike, likely to lose share to branded players like Jyoti who can enforce price hikes. |
| Intensifying brand wars and trade marketing spend (6-7% of sales) | Regional/Niche Adhesive Brands | loser | Med | Jyoti's aggressive celebrity endorsement and loyalty program spend raises the barrier to entry, squeezing smaller regional players who cannot match the marketing intensity. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Promoter Holding] Promoter holding increased from 50.83% in Jun 2025 to 50.89% as on Sep 2025.
- [Advisor] Investor presentation prepared with support of Kaptify Consulting (Strategy & Investor Relations Consulting).
